about: Reviewed trade conventions the resolve loop may cite (RESOLVE-LOOP-RESEARCH.md section 6; owner decision 2026-10-19). A convention may only explain, choose what evidence code fetches next, or name an arithmetic pattern code applies to PRINTED labels. It never supplies a value or a tolerance, and never overrides the architect's drawings or GV's rules (Raj's). It grows by review, never at run time: live web search results are saved as proposals only.

conventions.rule: EQ marks split a printed span into equal parts; each part is the printed span divided by the number of parts, only when the parts sit end to end on the span's own extension lines.
AFF means above finished floor (the end is the floor); CL means a centre line (the end is the centre of an outlet, sink or appliance).
A height to the underside of a top plus the top's printed thickness, on the same dimension line and touching end to end, is the height to the top of the counter.
conventions.approved_by: Anant (reading rule; Right only, owner decision 2026-10-19)

conventions.topic: A splash band inside a height
conventions.rule: A backsplash band printed on the same dimension line as a height, touching it end to end, moves that end from the counter's top to the splash's top.
conventions.approved_by: Anant (reading rule; Right only, owner decision 2026-10-19)

conventions.topic: A run to a box or bulkhead above the unit
conventions.rule: A dimension that runs to a soffit, bulkhead or box above the unit measures room context, not the millwork: another trade or different points.
VIF, field verify and plus-or-minus marks ask for site measurement: the item is Not compared (field verify), never red.
NIC, by others and by GC mark another trade's work: never a millwork difference.
Printed dimensions govern over scaled ones; a larger-scale drawing or detail over a smaller one; a later round over an earlier one.
conventions.approved_by: Anant (reading rule; GV's R2 and R3)

conventions.rule: On the vendor's sheets a value in brackets after millimetres is the same size in inches; it is not a reference dimension in the mechanical-drawing sense.
Typical sizes (a counter height, a top's thickness, a filler width) are background only: never a value, never a reason for a difference, never a tolerance.
